?:?:_Z14eval_far_batchPN4gicc9DeviceCtxE.rationale: grid_blocks=8 matches proxy_worker_lanes=8, so 8x64=512 ops split into 64 per lane: 5.37+2.872*64 ~= 189us versus host-serial staging 7.88+1.033*512 ~= 537us for trigger. Proxy lane parallelism dominates trigger's cheaper per-op stage; large flops_to_first_use (5392) hides issue latency either way.

?:?:_Z16eval_reuse_batchPN4gicc9DeviceCt.rationale: grid_blocks=1 gives no proxy lane parallelism: 32 loop-bound ops cost 5.37+2.872*32 ~= 97us by proxy versus 7.88+1.033*32 ~= 41us by trigger. descriptor_reusable=true and bound_known=true favor host descriptor reconstruction with batched DWQ release.

?:?:_Z16eval_tiny_singlePN4gicc9DeviceCt.rationale: Single 256B op, no loop: proxy 5.37+2.872=8.24us versus trigger 7.88+1.033=8.91us. The sub-microsecond gap is within noise, so evidence is too weak to pin a lowering; keep the IPC_OR_DWQ baseline.

?:?:_Z17eval_large_singlePN4gicc9DeviceC.rationale: 1MiB per block at 24 GB/s is ~44us/op (~350us aggregate over 8 blocks), dwarfing the ~8-9us issue overhead of either path; the proxy/trigger delta is bandwidth-masked, so abstain.

?:?:_Z19eval_adjacent_batchPN4gicc9Devic.rationale: grid_blocks=1 means one proxy lane: 16 known-bound ops cost 5.37+2.872*16 ~= 51us by proxy versus 7.88+1.033*16 ~= 24.4us by trigger. Coalescable const-size batch with known trip count offsets trigger's higher fixed cost; small flops_to_first_use only marginally counters this.

?:?:_Z19eval_dynamic_offsetPN4gicc9Devic.rationale: Only legal action: hk_capable=false and max_vector_bytes=1 with a runtime offset block compile-time descriptor reconstruction, so the device op must be preserved with CPU proxy work.

?:?:_Z21eval_static4_parallelPN4gicc9Dev.rationale: Four independent static sites x 4 grid_blocks = 16 producers over 8 proxy lanes (~2 ops/lane: 5.37+2*2.872 ~= 11.1us) versus host-serial trigger staging of all 16 ops (7.88+16*1.033 ~= 24.4us). Platform note allows distinct lanes for independent static sites.

Identical facts to its sibling static site: single op, grid_blocks=4, distinct proxy lanes available. Concurrent proxy issue across 8 lanes (~11us) beats serialized host staging of the full 16-op set (~24us).

Same static-parallel shape (batch_size=1, grid_blocks=4, const 4096B); keeping all four sites on proxy exploits min(grid_blocks, 8) lane concurrency instead of funneling every descriptor through one host staging stream.
Same static-parallel shape as its three siblings; uniform proxy assignment maximizes lane usage (2 ops/lane, ~11us) versus host-serial trigger staging of 16 ops (~24.4us).
